request.spec:
A name or alias may no longer be used on a sheet when any sheet of its tree (its ancestors, its
descendants and their descendants, among the sheets that exist) already uses it as a name or alias:
adding, renaming, an alias, the quick-add bar, the paste box and the import are refused as a
duplicate would be. People who already clash are not changed: each shows clashing yes, and every
edit of them through the person form is refused until the edit renames them to a name that does not
clash (and leaves no clashing alias).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A name or alias may no longer be used on a sheet when any sheet of its tree (its ancestors, its
descendants and their descendants, among the sheets that exist) already uses it as a name or alias:
adding, renaming, an alias, the quick-add bar, the paste box and the import are refused as a
duplicate would be. People who already clash are not changed: each shows clashing yes, and every
edit of them through the person form is refused until the edit renames them to a name that does not
clash (and leaves no clashing alias).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've made the change: names and aliases are now unique across a sheet's whole tree, and people who already clash show it. On a full `bin/e2e` run, 2 of the 4 tests pass (the main "uniqueness across tree" test and scenario 2). The other two fail on spec lines that I think are wrong, and my change doesn't reach either of them.

**What changed**
- **Server, `PersonService`:** a name or alias is refused if it's already used as a name or alias on any ancestor or any descendant of the sheet, ignoring case. This applies to adding a person, renaming, adding an alias, and the quick-add bar. The paste box already refuses any name that isn't on the sheet itself, so a name from elsewhere in the tree can't get through it. A refusal returns the existing "name in use" error and writes nothing to the store or the audit file.
- **Editing a clashing person:** every person-form edit is refused until it renames them to a name that's free across the tree, and none of their aliases clash either.
- **Showing clashes:** each person's data now carries a `clashing` flag, and their row shows `person-clashing` as `yes` or `no`. Two new queries in `PersonRepository` fetch the names and aliases used on the other sheets. Changing a sheet's parent doesn't alter anyone; existing clashes just show `yes`.
- **Front end:** a "Clashing" column in the people table, and the person-form error now reads "already in use on this sheet or its tree."

**The two failing tests**
- **Scenario 1** gets as far as line 232, which expects `sheet-parent` to show the literal text `__SHEET__-p` (line 319 has the same). That's a placeholder that was never replaced with the real sheet id, so no app can pass it. When I ran a temporary copy with the placeholder filled in, it stopped earlier, at line 177: a viewer trying to edit a claim, where the screen showed neither a result nor an error. That step passed in the full run but failed twice on its own. I didn't touch that code; I deleted the copy afterwards.
- **Scenario 3** never sets a parent, so it doesn't exercise this change. At line 902 it expects a three-line paste to be refused. The paste goes through the existing claim rules, which accept every line (Ada's 0.40 claim, for instance, is due on 1 April, after the closed P2 period). The audit log confirms the claims were added. Either the spec's data is off or the claim rules differ from what it assumes; I haven't changed either.

**Gaps**
- The change request mentions an import, but this app has no people import. `importPeople` exists in the test helpers but nothing in the app uses it, so there was nothing to change.
- Past-date ("as of") views always show clashing as `no`, because those saved snapshots don't record it.
- Bulk grade, merge and transfer aren't blocked for clashing people, since the request only names the person form.

**Port note:** your environment sets `PORT=3001`, and another java server, apparently from a different run, is already using 3001 and 3003. I left those alone and ran with `PORT=3017 bin/e2e`. Plain `bin/e2e` will test against whatever is on 3001.
